prompt: A worker uses their own tools, is paid per project, and serves several clients. They are most likely a(n):
explanation: Own tools, paid by the project, and more than one business are contractor factors on the common-law test.

prompt: Part-time workers who resign can buy continued health coverage under:
explanation: Following resignation, part-time workers are eligible to purchase health insurance under COBRA rules.

prompt: Contingent (flexible) workers are individuals who:
options: Do not have an implicit or explicit contract for ongoing employment
explanation: Flexible/contingent workers do not have an implicit or explicit contract for ongoing employment; core employees plan on long-term relationships.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: Someone who won’t continue employment because they are returning to school is:
explanation: People who do not expect to continue for personal reasons such as returning to school or retirement are not contingent workers.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: Two or more part-timers performing one job is called:
explanation: Job sharing: reduces costs, increases flexibility, maintains productivity, may increase loyalty.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: Which is NOT a listed reason for the rise in flexible workers?
options: Shift from manufacturing to a service economy
explanation: The slide lists recessions, international competition, and the shift from manufacturing to a service economy.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: About what share of part-time workers have retirement benefits, vs full-time?
explanation: Retirement benefits: about 38% of part-time workers compared to 81% of full-time workers.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: Employers must let part-timers join retirement plans after they meet the age and service requirements of:
explanation: Part-time workers must be allowed to participate after fulfilling the ERISA age and service requirements.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: Part-time workers are NOT protected under:
explanation: Health insurance: part-time workers are not protected under PPACA.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: Flextime, compressed workweeks and telecommuting are examples of:
explanation: Flexible work schedules: flextime, compressed workweeks, telecommuting.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: When flexible employees work during holidays, companies must:
explanation: Treatment of paid time off for holidays: companies must provide alternative time off.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: Under the COMMON-LAW test, a worker paid by the hour, supervised, using the employer’s tools is:
explanation: Employee if the employer controls/supervises, provides tools and location, and pays by the hour or time worked.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: Which factor appears in the ECONOMIC REALITIES test?
explanation: Economic realities factors: integration, investment in facilities, right to control, risk (profit or loss), skill, continuing relationship.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: A worker with a substantial investment in the work facilities and equipment points toward:
explanation: Economic realities test: substantial investment in facilities and equipment → contractor.
source: Written from Slides 10 · Executives & Flexible Workforce

prompt: Which of the following individuals is NOT a contingent worker?
options: A seasonal warehouse worker hired through December 31
An employee who plans to leave in May to return to graduate school
A consultant engaged for a six-month project
explanation: Leaving for personal reasons (school, retirement) does not make someone contingent. The prof repeated this in the video.

prompt: A leased employee is legally the employee of:
options: The client organization where the work is performed
explanation: The staffing agency. The client pays the agency; the agency pays the worker.

prompt: Which is NOT one of the three reasons given for the rise in use of flexible workers?
options: The shift from manufacturing to a service economy
The passage of the Family and Medical Leave Act
explanation: The three are recessions, international competition, and the manufacturing-to-service shift.

prompt: Regarding benefits for part-time workers, which statement is correct?
options: Employers must offer them health insurance under PPACA
Employers must allow them into retirement plans once ERISA age and service requirements are met
They are ineligible for COBRA after resignation
Retirement is a legally required benefit for all workers
explanation: Must allow retirement participation once ERISA thresholds are met. Part-timers aren’t protected under PPACA, can buy COBRA, and retirement is discretionary.

prompt: “Investment in facilities” and “risk of profit or loss” are factors found in:
explanation: Economic realities test only. Those two never appear on the common-law list.

prompt: A compressed workweek most commonly takes the form of:
explanation: Four 10-hour days. Three 12-hour days (36 hours) also appears, but 4×10 is most common.

prompt: True or false: Part-time employees are considered contingent workers.
explanation: True. Part-timers are contingent workers.

prompt: True or false: Private organizations are legally required to close on federal holidays.
explanation: False. That’s exactly why the alternative-paid-time-off rule exists.

prompt: A retailer hires three workers for the holidays with a definite stop date. The stop date is what makes them:
explanation: No contract for ongoing employment → contingent.

prompt: Two part-timers split one full-time job. Which is NOT one of the four listed effects of job sharing?
explanation: The four: reduces costs, increases flexibility, maintains productivity, may increase loyalty. Job sharers typically aren’t benefit-eligible.

prompt: “Intent” and “method of payment” are factors on which test?
explanation: Intent, tools, supervision, method of payment, type of business, more than one firm → common law only.

prompt: An employee drops her kid off at 8:15, starts at 8:30, leaves at 3:15, and finishes her hours remotely. This is:
explanation: Working different times of the day = flextime.
